questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Particular Solution of an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+$ {{field-1}} $\cdot \,\,$ |  | $0$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}],
$$

where $a,b$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=-2{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ -2[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2a \\ -2b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-b \\ 4a\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2a \\ -2b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-b+1 \\ 4a-2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-b+1=-2a \\ 4a-2=-2b\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get 

$$
b=2a+1.
$$

 
Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $b,$ we have

$$
4a-2=-2(2a+1)\,⇒\,a=0.
$$

So, 

$$
b=2(0)+1=1.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is constant. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also constant, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-3t-4 \\ 2{t}^{2}+4t+3\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,+$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-3t \\ {t}^{2}+t+1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-3t \\ {t}^{2}+t+1\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2(0)} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0\cdot {e}^{2(0)} \\ {e}^{2(0)}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2\cdot {0}^{2}-3\cdot 0 \\ {0}^{2}+0+1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}+1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=-3 \\ {c}_{2}+1=3\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{1}=-3.$ From the second equation, we have ${c}_{2}=2.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=-3\cdot [\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-3t \\ {t}^{2}+t+1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}7\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,-$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0){e}^{-0} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0){e}^{-0}\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0){e}^{-0} \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0){e}^{-0}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0)\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+3 \\ -{c}_{2}+2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+3=7 \\ -{c}_{2}+2=7\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{1}=4.$ From the second equation, we have ${c}_{2}=-5.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=4\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]-5\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t){e}^{-t} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].
$$
